content:
According to Bloomberg's latest report, Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop. The company is reportedly "developing a prototype product," but has not yet decided whether to ultimately bring it to market.

The internal prototype reportedly features a "slim fabric band paired with a compute module containing built-in sensors." The project is currently in the "technical exploration" phase, and Bloomberg noted that the product is not expected to launch until at least 2028—if Apple ultimately decides to release it.

The project reportedly has the support of Apple's senior leadership, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took over Apple's health team last October following Jeff Williams's departure.

Products like Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among users who want to track health and fitness data without wearing a smartwatch. According to Reuters, Oura is preparing for an IPO and recently announced it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ending June 30. Revenue grew 74% to $1.21 billion in the nine months ending June 30.

However, Apple remains the dominant player in the smartwatch market. The Apple Watch also offers a richer set of features than health-and-fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.
